mainTopic: Sources that קרבנות ציבור override שבת and טומאה, and whether the משנה fits רבי יהושע's view that blood and meat depend on each other
overview: The גמרא explains why the משנה lists the goats of ראש חודש: we might have thought ראש חודש is not a מועד, and אביי's פסוק from איכה shows that it is. A ברייתא then gives the sources that קרבנות ציבור override שבת and טומאה. The source for the תמיד and the פסח is במועדו. The source for the other קרבנות ציבור is ״אלה תעשו לה׳ במועדיכם״. The source for the עומר and the שתי הלחם is ״וידבר משה את מעדי ה׳״. A צריכותא shows that each source is needed, because each offering has a feature the others lack. Next the גמרא sets out two assumptions. The first is that טומאה is only דחויה בציבור, so the ציץ is needed; only רבי יהודה holds הותרה. The second is that the ציץ does not make impure meat permitted to eat; only רבי אליעזר disagrees. On that basis it suggests that our משנה does not follow רבי יהושע, who holds that blood and meat depend on each other, against רבי אליעזר, who holds that blood alone is enough.

steps.title: Why the משנה needed to list the ראש חודש goats
steps.stepSummary: The משנה had to mention שעירי ראשי חדשים. Otherwise we might think ראש חודש is not a מועד, so its קרבנות would not override טומאה. The משנה teaches that ראש חודש is called a מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The goats of ראש חודש had to be mentioned. You might have thought that, since the word 'מועד' is not written about them, they are different. So the משנה teaches us that ראש חודש is also called a מועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה bothered to include the ראש חודש goats in its list of offerings that may be brought in טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קרבנות ציבור override טומאה because they have a fixed time, called a מועד. The Torah never uses the word מועד for ראש חודש, so we might have left its goats out of this rule. The משנה includes them to teach that ראש חודש also counts as a מועד.

keyTerms.meaning: The goats brought as sin-offerings on ראש חודש
It was necessary for him (the משנה) to say it
It might have entered your mind to say (a mistaken first assumption)
It teaches us (the actual lesson)
An appointed, fixed time

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the question is whether ראש חודש goats are קרבנות ציבור. They clearly are. The question is only whether ראש חודש has the status of a מועד, which is what lets these offerings override טומאה.

phrases.english: The goats of the New Moons — it was necessary for him (to mention them),
phrases.notes: The גמרא is answering a question it doesn't say out loud: why mention them at all?

phrases.english: it could enter your mind to say
phrases.notes: This sets up an idea that turns out to be wrong.

phrases.english: 'appointed time' is not written about them,
phrases.notes: So perhaps they don't override טומאה

phrases.english: so it teaches us
that the New Moon is called an appointed time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the implied question of why the משנה needed to list the ראש חודש goats.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did the משנה need to list שעירי ראשי חדשים?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: To teach that ראש חודש counts as a מועד even though the Torah does not use that word for it.

steps.title: אביי's verse shows ראש חודש is called a מועד
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the month of תמוז in the year of the מרגלים had thirty days. He brings the pasuk ״קרא עלי מועד״, which calls the setting of the new month a מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: This matches what אביי said: They made תמוז of that year a full month (30 days), as it is written, 'He proclaimed a מועד against me to crush my young men.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the claim that ראש חודש is called a מועד. It does this with a teaching of אביי that uses a pasuk from איכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי needed תמוז to have 30 days so that the forty days of the מרגלים would end on the night of תשעה באב. The pasuk says 'He proclaimed a מועד against me.' This refers to fixing the new month, which set up that sad day. So the pasuk uses the word מועד for a ראש חודש.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with what אביי said
They made it full, a 30-day month
He proclaimed an appointed time against me (איכה א:טו)
My young men

phrases.english: In line with Abaye, for Abaye said:
Tammuz of that year — they filled it out (made it 30 days),
as it is written: 'He proclaimed an appointed time against me'
'to crush my young men.'
phrases.notes: Here the new month that was announced is called a מועד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim in step 1 that ראש חודש is called a מועד.
steps.raayaObject: That ראש חודש is called a מועד
steps.raayaSupportSource: אביי's reading of ״קרא עלי מועד״ (איכה א:טו), about the 30-day תמוז in the year of the מרגלים
steps.whyThisMatters: Once ראש חודש is a מועד, its goats override טומאה just like other fixed-time קרבנות ציבור.

steps.title: Where do we learn that everything depends on מועד?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source showing that all these קרבנות ציבור override טומאה because of the word מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that all of them come from the word 'מועד'? Where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask for the source behind the idea it just used: that the word מועד is what lets all communal offerings override טומאה. This sets up the ברייתא that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 1–2 took it for granted that having a מועד is the key. Here the גמרא asks where that rule comes from for all the offerings, not just the ones where the Torah says במועדו.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say?
All of them
From where do we know these things?

phrases.english: Is that to say that all of them come from 'appointed time'?
From where are these matters derived?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּכוּלְּהוּ מִ״מּוֹעֵד״ אָתוּ, מְנָהָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the idea that steps 1–2 relied on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that all קרבנות ציבור override שבת and טומאה because of מועד.

steps.title: The ברייתא: תמיד and פסח override because of 'in its appointed time'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks why the pasuk ״וידבר משה את מעדי ה׳״ is needed. It explains that from the word במועדו we had only learned about the תמיד and the פסח: they are brought even on שבת and even in טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'And משה declared the appointed times of ה׳.' Why does the pasuk say this? Because so far we had only learned this about the תמיד and the פסח, where it says 'in its appointed time.' 'In its appointed time' means even on שבת. 'In its appointed time' means even in טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא first explains what we already know: the תמיד and the פסח override שבת and טומאה because the Torah says במועדו about them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word במועדו teaches that the fixed time must be kept no matter what, even when it falls on שבת or when people are in טומאה. But this word appears only about the תמיד and the פסח. The ברייתא now needs a source for the other offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: What does the pasuk come to teach?
The daily communal offering
In its appointed time
Ritual impurity

steps.confusionAlert: Step 5 quotes a second פסוק for the other offerings, but the ברייתא is not finished yet. Step 6 explains why ״וידבר משה את מעדי ה׳״ is still needed: it covers the עומר and the שתי הלחם.

phrases.english: As the Sages taught:
'And Moses declared the appointed times of the Lord' —
what does the verse come to teach?

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁלֹּא לָמַדְנוּ אֶלָּא לְתָמִיד וּפֶסַח
phrases.english: Because we only learned about the daily offering and the Paschal lamb
that 'in its appointed time' is said about them,
'in its appointed time' — even on Shabbat,
'in its appointed time' — even in ritual impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: וַיְדַבֵּר מֹשֶׁה אֶת מֹעֲדֵי ה׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering step 3 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word במועדו teaches that the תמיד and the פסח override שבת and טומאה.

steps.title: Extending the rule to all other communal offerings
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks where we learn this rule for the other קרבנות ציבור. It answers with ״אלה תעשו לה׳ במועדיכם״.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do we learn this for the other communal offerings? As it says: 'These you shall offer to ה׳ in your appointed times.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues. It extends the 'override שבת and טומאה' rule to every קרבן ציבור, using a pasuk that speaks of all the offerings of the מועדים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This pasuk comes at the end of the list of holiday מוספין. Its word במועדיכם covers all of them together. That is how the word מועד becomes the shared basis for all communal offerings overriding טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings brought on behalf of the whole community
From where do we know?
In your appointed times (במדבר כט:לט)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source behind the משנה's whole list. Every communal offering with a fixed time overrides טומאה because of the word במועדיכם.

phrases.english: The rest of the communal offerings — from where?
As it is stated: 'These you shall offer to the Lord in your appointed times.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא, moving from the תמיד and פסח to all קרבנות ציבור.
steps.raayaObject: That all קרבנות ציבור override שבת and טומאה

steps.title: Including the עומר and the שתי הלחם from the פסוק of מעדי ה׳
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds the עומר, the שתי הלחם, and the קרבנות brought with them. It learns this from ״וידבר משה את מעדי ה׳ אל בני ישראל״, which puts all the מועדים into one group.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we include the עומר and what is brought with it, and the שתי הלחם and what is brought with them? The pasuk says: 'And משה spoke the appointed times of ה׳ to בני ישראל.' The pasuk made them all one מועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its list. It now adds the עומר, the שתי הלחם, and their קרבנות to the group of קרבנות that override שבת and טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These קרבנות are written in פרשת אמור (ויקרא כג). They are not in the list of מוסף offerings in פרשת פנחס, which the pasuk ״אלה תעשו״ covers. So they need their own source. The closing pasuk of פרשת אמור groups every מועד together, so all of these קרבנות share the same 'מועד' status.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley offering brought on the 16th of ניסן, together with a lamb as an עולה
The two wheat loaves brought on שבועות, together with lambs and other קרבנות
'The pasuk teaches' – introduces the source
One appointed-time status for all of them

steps.confusionAlert: ״וידבר משה את מעדי ה׳״ is the same pasuk the ברייתא asked about in Step 4. Here we finally see what it is needed for: the עומר and the שתי הלחם.

phrases.english: From where do we include the omer and what is offered with it,
the two loaves and what is offered with them?
The verse teaches:
'And Moses declared the appointed times of the Lord
to the children of Israel,'
the verse established one appointed time for all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's list after the other קרבנות ציבור were derived from ״אלה תעשו״.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the עומר, the שתי הלחם, and their accompanying קרבנות override שבת and טומאה
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא כג:מד – ״וידבר משה את מעדי ה׳ אל בני ישראל״

steps.title: Why are all these sources needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the Torah needs separate sources for the תמיד, the פסח, and the other קרבנות. One source should be enough to teach the rule for all of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need all of these?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's many sources. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא explains why each one is necessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the Torah does not repeat itself without a reason. If one קרבן ציבור overrides שבת and טומאה, we could seemingly learn all the others from it. So the extra sources look unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Why do I need all of these?' – a challenge that the extra sources seem unnecessary

phrases.english: And why do I need all of these?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the need for the several sources the ברייתא just listed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of three separate sources: במועדו, ״אלה תעשו״, and ״וידבר משה את מעדי ה׳״
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One source should be enough. The other קרבנות could be learned from it, so the extra sources look like repetition.

steps.title: Why we could not learn the פסח from the תמיד
steps.stepSummary: All the sources are needed. If the Torah wrote only the תמיד, we would say it is special because it is frequent and fully burned. Then the פסח would not override.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are needed. If the Torah wrote only the תמיד, I would say the תמיד is different, because it is frequent and entirely burned. But the פסח would not override. So the Torah teaches us the פסח too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer. It shows that the תמיד alone could not teach us about the פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תמיד has two stringent features. It is brought every day (תדיר), and it is completely burned on the מזבח (כליל). The פסח has neither feature, so we might think it is weaker and does not override שבת and טומאה. That is why the Torah needs to write the פסח separately.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They are necessary' – introduces a צריכותא explaining why each source is needed
'I would have said' – the mistaken assumption we would otherwise make
Frequent – brought regularly, every day
Entirely burned on the מזבח
'It teaches us' – the extra source comes to rule out the mistake

phrases.english: They are necessary, for if the Merciful One had written only the daily offering,
I would have said the daily offering is different,
since it is frequent and entirely burned,
but the Paschal offering — not,
so it teaches us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First part of the answer to the challenge in Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא – each source is needed because each קרבן has its own unique feature
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the תמיד overrides, because it is frequent and fully burned. The פסח would not override.
steps.terutzMaskana: A separate source shows that the פסח also overrides שבת and טומאה.

steps.title: Why we could not learn the תמיד from the פסח
steps.stepSummary: If the Torah wrote only the פסח, we would say it overrides because skipping it brings כרת. The תמיד has no כרת, so we would think it does not override.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the Torah wrote only the פסח, I would say the פסח overrides because skipping it is punished with כרת. But the תמיד, which has no כרת, would not override. So the Torah teaches us the תמיד too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the other direction. The פסח alone could not teach us about the תמיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסח has its own stringency. Someone who does not bring it is punished with כרת, and the תמיד has no such punishment. Since each קרבן has a strength the other lacks, neither can be learned from the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Punished with כרת (spiritual cutting off) for failing to do it
'I would say not' – it does not override
'The Merciful One' – a name for the Torah or ה׳

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written only the Paschal offering,
I would say the Paschal offering overrides, since it carries the punishment of karet,
but the daily offering, which does not carry karet —
say it does not override,
so it teaches us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second part of the צריכותא, reversing the direction of Step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the פסח overrides, because skipping it is punished with כרת.
steps.terutzMaskana: A separate source shows that the תמיד also overrides.

steps.title: Why the other communal offerings need their own source
steps.stepSummary: Even with both the תמיד and the פסח written, we would say only these two override, because each has a stringent feature. So the Torah wrote ״אלה תעשו לה׳ במועדיכם״ for all the other קרבנות ציבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the Torah wrote only these two, I would say only these override, because each has a strict side. The תמיד is frequent and fully burned. The פסח carries כרת. But the other קרבנות ציבור would not override. So the Torah wrote: 'These you shall offer to ה׳ in your appointed times.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer. It explains why the other קרבנות ציבור need their own pasuk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two examples are still not enough. Both the תמיד and the פסח have a strict feature (צד חמור). We might say that only a strict קרבן overrides, so the ordinary קרבנות ציבור would not. The pasuk ״אלה תעשו לה׳ במועדיכם״ teaches that they override too.

keyTerms.meaning: These two (the תמיד and the פסח)
A stringent feature
The rest of the communal offerings
'In your appointed times' – the word teaching that they override

steps.whatToRemember: Each source is needed. The תמיד is frequent and fully burned. The פסח carries כרת. The other קרבנות ציבור have neither feature, so they need ״אלה תעשו לה׳ במועדיכם״. The עומר and the שתי הלחם need ״וידבר משה את מעדי ה׳״.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic example of the גמרא's צריכותא pattern. A קרבן with a special stringency cannot teach a rule to a קרבן without that stringency.

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written only these two,
I would have said it is only these that override,
because they have a stringent aspect:
the daily offering is frequent and entirely burned,
the Paschal offering carries the punishment of karet.
But the rest of the communal offerings —
say they do not override,
so the Merciful One wrote:
'These you shall offer to the Lord in your appointed times.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final part of the צריכותא. It explains why the source from Step 5 is needed even after the תמיד and the פסח.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only strict קרבנות (the תמיד and the פסח) override. Ordinary קרבנות ציבור do not.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״אלה תעשו לה׳ במועדיכם״ teaches that all קרבנות ציבור override שבת and טומאה.

steps.title: The general verse alone would not cover the עומר and שתי הלחם
steps.stepSummary: If the Torah had written only ״אלה תעשו לה׳ במועדיכם״, we would apply it only to communal offerings that atone. We would leave out the עומר and שתי הלחם, which only 'permit.' So the extra source is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the Torah had written only 'These you shall do for ה׳ in your appointed times,' I would have said this covers only the other communal offerings that come to atone. But the עומר and the שתי הלחם do not come to atone. They only come to permit, so they would not override. That is why the Torah teaches them separately.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps explaining why every source is needed. Here it shows that the general verse for the communal offerings would not be enough to include the עומר and the שתי הלחם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Offerings that atone (כפרה) seem important enough to override שבת and טומאה. The עומר and שתי הלחם do not atone. They only make something allowed: the עומר permits eating new grain, and the שתי הלחם permit bringing new grain in the מקדש. Without their own source (״וידבר משה את מעדי ה׳״), we would think this weaker purpose cannot override.

keyTerms.meaning: to atone for sin
to permit (make something allowed)
merely, only
it teaches us (the verse is needed to tell us otherwise)

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written
'These you shall do for ה׳ in your appointed times,'
phrases.notes: The source for the other communal offerings (step 10).

phrases.english: I would have said
only the other communal offerings that come to atone (override).
But the Omer and the Two Loaves,
which do not come to atone,
but merely come to permit,
would not override. So it teaches us (that they do).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא: ״אֵלֶּה תַּעֲשׂוּ לַה׳ בְּמוֹעֲדֵיכֶם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the chain of answers to the קשיא in step 7, now explaining why the עומר and שתי הלחם need their own source.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only offerings that atone override; the עומר and שתי הלחם, which merely permit, do not.
steps.terutzMaskana: The separate verse ״וידבר משה את מעדי ה׳״ teaches that the עומר and שתי הלחם also override.

steps.title: The עומר and שתי הלחם alone would not cover the other offerings
steps.stepSummary: If the Torah had written only the עומר and שתי הלחם, we would say the opposite: they are stronger because they permit, and the other offerings would not override. So both sources are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the Torah had written only the עומר and the שתי הלחם, I would have said the opposite. The עומר and שתי הלחם are stronger because they come to permit, so they override. But these other offerings would not. That is why the Torah teaches both.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא flips the last point around. It shows that the source for the עומר and שתי הלחם would not be enough to teach about the other communal offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same feature, 'coming to permit,' can be seen as a weakness or as a strength. If we only had the עומר and שתי הלחם, we could say they override because a whole category (new grain) depends on them. Then we would not extend the rule to other offerings. So each source covers something the other cannot, and the צריכותא is complete.

keyTerms.meaning: by themselves, alone
on the contrary
they are stronger / more important
these (the other offerings)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't be thrown by the flip. In step 11, 'coming to permit' made the עומר look weaker. Here the same feature makes it look stronger. The גמרא is showing that we could reason either way, so we need both verses.
steps.whatToRemember: Every source is needed: תמיד (frequent and fully burned), פסח (כרת), the other offerings (atone), and the עומר and שתי הלחם (permit). Each has its own feature, so none can be learned from the others.

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written
the Omer and the Two Loaves by themselves,
I would have said, on the contrary:
the Omer and the Two Loaves, which are stronger
because they come to permit (they override),
but these (other offerings) do not.
So it teaches us (each source separately).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא עוֹמֶר וּשְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם לְחוֹדַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The reverse of step 11. It completes the answer to the קשיא of step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the עומר and שתי הלחם override, because they permit; the other offerings do not.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both verses are needed, so all of these communal offerings override שבת and טומאה.

steps.title: Initial assumption: impurity is only pushed aside for the community
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים first assumed that everyone agrees טומאה is only דחויה בציבור, so the ציץ is needed to make the offering acceptable.
steps.simpleTranslation: They assumed that everyone agrees: טומאה is only 'pushed aside' for the community, not fully permitted. So the ציץ of the כהן גדול is needed to make the offering acceptable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic and sets up a starting assumption. Later steps will build on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to understand why a ציבור may bring offerings while טמא. 'דחויה' means the prohibition still exists but gives way, so the ציץ is needed to fix the problem. 'הותרה' means the prohibition simply does not apply to the ציבור. The word ״סברוה״ tells us this is only what they first assumed, and it may be questioned later.

keyTerms.meaning: they (the חכמים) assumed (often a view that will later be challenged)
impurity is 'pushed aside' for the community; the prohibition still exists but gives way
the gold plate on the forehead of the כהן גדול
to make (an offering) acceptable

steps.confusionAlert: ״סברוה״ is not the final ruling. It is a starting assumption, and the גמרא may overturn it later.
steps.whyThisMatters: The difference between דחויה and הותרה decides whether the ציץ is needed and how far the permission for the ציבור reaches.

phrases.english: They assumed
that according to everyone
ritual impurity is overridden (pushed aside) for the community,
and the frontplate is required to make it acceptable.

steps.triggerLanguage: סַבְרוּהָ דִּלְכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא טוּמְאָה דְּחוּיָה הִיא בְּצִיבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. The earlier steps discussed offerings brought while טמא, and this step examines what kind of permission that is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The starting assumption is that everyone holds טומאה דחויה בציבור, so the ציץ is needed to make the offering acceptable.

steps.title: Only רבי יהודה is known to hold that impurity is fully permitted
steps.stepSummary: The assumption is explained: the only תנא we know of who says טומאה הותרה בציבור is רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because there is no תנא we have heard of who says טומאה is fully permitted for the community, except רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why it made the assumption in step 13. Everyone else holds דחויה, and only רבי יהודה stands apart. This sets up the ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption 'everyone agrees' really means everyone except one known תנא. By naming רבי יהודה as the only one who holds הותרה, the גמרא makes the assumption believable. The next step will show where רבי יהודה's view comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: a sage from the time of the משנה
whom you have heard (say this)
fully permitted; the prohibition does not apply at all

phrases.english: For there is no תנא you have heard of
who says ritual impurity is permitted for the community
except רבי יהודה,

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּלֵיכָּא תַּנָּא דְּשָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ דְּאָמַר טוּמְאָה הוּתְּרָה בְּצִיבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and narrows the 'everyone agrees' assumption of step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Among the known תנאים, only רבי יהודה holds טומאה הותרה בציבור.

steps.title: The ברייתא: does the frontplate work only when worn?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is the source. רבי שמעון says the ציץ makes the offering acceptable even when it is not on the כהן גדול's forehead. רבי יהודה says it works only while it is on his forehead.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: the ציץ makes the offering acceptable whether or not it is on his forehead. This is the view of רבי שמעון. רבי יהודה says: while it is still on his forehead, it makes the offering acceptable. When it is no longer on his forehead, it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that shows רבי יהודה's view, to back up the claim in step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה limits the ציץ: it helps only while the כהן גדול is actually wearing it. רבי שמעון says the ציץ works even when it is not worn. As the ברייתא continues (Steps 16–17), רבי יהודה states openly that טומאה הותרה בציבור, and from that exchange the גמרא infers that רבי שמעון holds דחויה (Step 18).

keyTerms.meaning: his forehead
makes (the offering) acceptable
it is still (in place)

steps.confusionAlert: This first part of the ברייתא does not yet say 'הותרה.' רבי יהודה only limits the ציץ to when it is worn. He states his view outright later in the same ברייתא (Step 17): ״שטומאה הותרה בציבור״.
steps.whyThisMatters: This makes רבי יהודה the main example of the הותרה view, which the following discussion will use.

phrases.english: As it was taught: the frontplate,
whether it is on his forehead
or not on his forehead, makes acceptable;
this is the view of רבי שמעון.
רבי יהודה says:
while it is still on his forehead, it makes acceptable;

phrases.aramaic: אֵין עוֹדֵיהוּ עַל מִצְחוֹ — אֵינוֹ מְרַצֶּה.
phrases.english: when it is no longer on his forehead, it does not make acceptable.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: צִיץ, בֵּין שֶׁיֶּשְׁנוֹ עַל מִצְחוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ברייתא behind the claim in step 14 that רבי יהודה holds הותרה.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה (alone) holds טומאה הותרה בציבור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא in which רבי שמעון and רבי יהודה argue about whether the ציץ works when it is not on the forehead.

steps.title: רבי שמעון proves his view from the כהן גדול on יום הכיפורים
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון argues that on יום הכיפורים the ציץ is not on the כהן גדול's forehead, yet it still makes the offering acceptable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said to him: The כהן גדול on יום הכיפורים will prove it. The ציץ is not on his forehead, and still it makes the offering acceptable.
steps.whatsHappening: We are still inside the ברייתא from Step 15. רבי שמעון brings a proof to his opinion that the ציץ works even when it is not on the forehead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום הכיפורים the כהן גדול serves for part of the day in four white garments, without the gold ציץ. Even so, impure communal offerings are accepted that day. So רבי שמעון concludes that the ציץ works even when it is not being worn.

keyTerms.meaning: will prove it (a case that shows the point)
his forehead
makes the offering acceptable
the High Priest

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said to him (to Rabbi Yehuda):
The High Priest on Yom Kippur will prove it,
phrases.notes: On יום הכיפורים he wears only the white garments for part of the service, with no ציץ.

phrases.english: for it is not on his forehead, and yet it makes the offering acceptable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from Step 15 with רבי שמעון's supporting proof.
steps.raayaObject: The ציץ works even when it is not on the forehead.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of the כהן גדול on יום הכיפורים, who serves part of the day without the ציץ.

steps.title: רבי יהודה rejects the יום הכיפורים proof
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה answers that יום הכיפורים proves nothing, because in his view טומאה is fully permitted for the community.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Leave יום הכיפורים aside, because טומאה is fully permitted for the community.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה pushes away רבי שמעון's proof. He says the יום הכיפורים offerings are communal, and communal offerings do not need the ציץ at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, טומאה is completely permitted in communal offerings, so nothing needs to be 'fixed.' That is why there is no need for the ציץ on יום הכיפורים. So the case shows nothing about whether the ציץ works when it is not worn.

keyTerms.meaning: leave it aside; that case is different
fully permitted when it concerns the community

phrases.english: He said to him: Leave Yom Kippur aside,
for impurity is fully permitted for the community.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from יום הכיפורים, not רבי שמעון's whole opinion.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Communal offerings need no ציץ at all if טומאה is fully permitted, so the case is not relevant.

steps.title: So רבי שמעון holds impurity is only set aside for the community
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא learns from the debate that רבי שמעון holds טומאה is only דחויה בציבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: We can learn from this that רבי שמעון holds that טומאה is only set aside for the community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof it began in Step 14. Since רבי יהודה's answer depends on 'הותרה,' רבי שמעון must hold 'דחויה.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון brought יום הכיפורים as a case where the ציץ was needed. That only makes sense if communal טומאה still needs fixing, meaning it is only דחויה. This confirms that רבי יהודה is the only one who says הותרה, so the first assumption from Step 13 holds.

keyTerms.meaning: by inference; we can learn from this
set aside but not fully permitted

steps.whatToRemember: Only רבי יהודה says טומאה הותרה בציבור. רבי שמעון holds דחויה, so the ציץ is needed to make communal offerings acceptable.

phrases.english: By inference, Rabbi Shimon holds:
Impurity is only set aside for the community.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the exchange in Steps 16-17.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי שמעון holds טומאה דחויה בציבור, so the first assumption from Step 13 holds for everyone except רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Second assumption: the ציץ does not cover the eaten parts
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים also assumed that everyone agrees the ציץ does not make impure meat permitted to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to everyone, the ציץ does not make things acceptable regarding eating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second background assumption, alongside the one in Step 13. Both are setting up the question that comes in Step 22.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ציץ can fix the offering itself so that it counts on the altar. But it cannot make impure meat permitted to eat. So an impure offering may be valid, yet its meat still may not be eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: according to everyone
the parts of offerings that are eaten

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'the offering is accepted' with 'the meat may be eaten.' The ציץ handles the first, not the second.

phrases.english: And according to everyone,
the frontplate does not make things acceptable regarding the eaten parts,

steps.triggerLanguage: וּדְכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אֵין הַצִּיץ מְרַצֶּה עַל אֲכִילוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second shared assumption parallel to the first one in Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ציץ does not make impure eaten portions acceptable to eat.

steps.title: Only רבי אליעזר disagrees
steps.stepSummary: The assumption is explained: the only תנא who says the ציץ covers eaten parts is רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: For there is no תנא we have heard say that the ציץ makes things acceptable regarding eating, except רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why it calls this view 'everyone.' Only one תנא disagrees, so in general this is the accepted view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This step has the same pattern as Step 14. There, only רבי יהודה held the other view. Here, only רבי אליעזר holds the other view, and he is a lone opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: there is no תנא
whom you have heard say

phrases.english: For there is no tanna you have heard
who says the frontplate makes things acceptable regarding eaten parts
except Rabbi Eliezer,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the basis for the assumption in Step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר is the only one who holds the ציץ covers eaten portions.

steps.title: The ברייתא: רבי אליעזר versus רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי אליעזר says the ציץ covers eaten parts, and רבי יוסי says it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר says the ציץ makes things acceptable regarding eating. רבי יוסי says the ציץ does not make things acceptable regarding eating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for what it said in Step 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that רבי אליעזר does hold this view. It also shows that רבי יוסי disagrees with him. This backs up the claim that the main view is that the ציץ does not cover the eaten parts.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
The frontplate makes things acceptable regarding eaten parts.
Rabbi Yosei says:
The frontplate does not make things acceptable regarding eaten parts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ברייתא source for Step 20.
steps.raayaObject: Only רבי אליעזר holds that the ציץ covers eaten parts.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי אליעזר and רבי יוסי.
steps.whatToRemember: Two assumptions are now in place. First, טומאה is only דחויה בציבור, so the ציץ is needed. Second, the ציץ does not make impure meat permitted to eat.

steps.title: Suggestion: our משנה does not follow רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: Based on these two assumptions, the גמרא suggests that our משנה goes against רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say that our משנה does not follow רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now uses the two assumptions to raise a problem. It suggests that our משנה disagrees with רבי יהושע, and the next step brings the source for this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says that certain communal offerings are brought in טומאה even though they may not be eaten. If the meat cannot be eaten, and someone holds that blood and meat depend on each other, the blood should not be offered either. So the משנה seems to clash with רבי יהושע.

keyTerms.meaning: shall we say? (introduces a suggestion)
not in accordance with

phrases.english: Shall we say that our Mishnah
is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the two assumptions to raise a new challenge to the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that communal offerings are brought in טומאה but not eaten.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the meat may not be eaten, then according to רבי יהושע the blood may not be offered either. So the offering could not be brought at all.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: blood and meat depend on each other
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא on the verse 'הבשר והדם' shows that רבי יהושע holds the offering needs both valid blood and valid meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'And you shall offer your burnt offerings, the meat and the blood.' רבי יהושע says: If there is no blood, there is no meat. If there is no meat, there is no blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רבי יהושע's view. This explains why the משנה seems to disagree with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע reads the verse as linking meat and blood together. If the meat is impure or lost, the blood may not be thrown on the מזבח. Since the ציץ does not fix the eaten meat, the impure meat counts as 'no meat.' So according to רבי יהושע, the blood should not be offered.

keyTerms.meaning: your burnt offerings
the meat and the blood
if there is no blood, there is no meat

steps.whyThisMatters: This link between blood and meat is what makes the problem real. Without it, an offering whose meat cannot be eaten could still be offered on the מזבח.

phrases.english: As it was taught: 'And you shall offer your burnt offerings, the meat and the blood,'
Rabbi Yehoshua says:
If there is no (valid) blood, there is no (valid) meat;
if there is no (valid) meat, there is no (offering of the) blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ברייתא source for the challenge in Step 22.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהושע holds that blood and meat depend on each other.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא on the verse 'ועשית עולתיך הבשר והדם'.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: Blood works even without meat
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues with רבי אליעזר's opposing view. Blood brings כפרה even if there is no valid meat, and 'הבשר והדם' teaches that the meat is thrown like the blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: the blood works even if there is no meat, as it says, 'And the blood of your offerings shall be poured out.' So what do I do with the verse 'And you shall make your burnt-offerings, the meat and the blood'? It comes to tell you: just as blood is thrown, so too meat is thrown.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא from Step 23. Here רבי אליעזר disagrees with רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר learns from 'ודם זבחיך ישפך' that the blood is the main part of the offering, so it works even when the meat is gone or invalid. He still has to explain the verse רבי יהושע used, 'הבשר והדם'. He says that verse is not about needing both. It compares how the meat and the blood are placed on the מזבח: both are thrown (זריקה).

keyTerms.meaning: 'And the blood of your offerings shall be poured out' (דברים יב:כז)
'How do I uphold…?' Asks what a verse teaches, according to this view
Throwing (of blood, and here of meat) onto the מזבח
Even though there is no (valid) meat

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר does not ignore the verse 'הבשר והדם'. He uses it for a different lesson: how the meat is offered, not whether the meat is required for כפרה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: blood —
even though there is no meat,
as it says: 'And the blood of your offerings shall be poured out,'
and how do I uphold
'And you shall make your burnt-offerings, the meat and the blood'?
It comes to tell you: just as blood is by throwing,
so too meat is by throwing.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: דָּם — אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בָּשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא from Step 23 with the opposing view of רבי אליעזר.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר holds blood alone brings כפרה, unlike רבי יהושע.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's reading of 'ודם זבחיך ישפך' and 'הבשר והדם'.

steps.title: A small gap between the ramp and the altar
steps.stepSummary: Since the meat must be thrown, there must have been a small gap between the כבש and the מזבח to throw it across.
steps.simpleTranslation: You must say: there is a small gap between the ramp and the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: This draws a practical conclusion from רבי אליעזר's teaching that the meat is 'thrown.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the meat had to be thrown, the כהן could not simply walk up and place it down. So there must have been a small open space (לול) between the ramp and the מזבח. The כהן stood on the ramp and threw the meat across that space onto the fire.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You must say', a forced conclusion
A small gap or opening
The ramp leading up to the מזבח

phrases.english: You must say:

phrases.aramaic: לוּל קָטָן יֵשׁ בֵּין כֶּבֶשׁ לַמִּזְבֵּחַ.
phrases.english: there is a small gap between the ramp and the altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר: לוּל קָטָן יֵשׁ בֵּין כֶּבֶשׁ לַמִּזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a physical consequence from the rule 'אף בשר בזריקה'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because the meat is thrown, there is a small gap between the כבש and the מזבח.

steps.title: How does רבי יהושע handle the blood verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the verse 'ודם זבחיך ישפך' shows that blood is the main thing, so why doesn't רבי יהושע agree?
steps.simpleTranslation: And for רבי יהושע too, isn't it written: 'And the blood of your offerings shall be poured out'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יהושע with רבי אליעזר's verse. It asks how he can ignore it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's source seems to show clearly that blood alone is enough. רבי יהושע requires valid meat too, so he seems to go against this verse. The question is aimed at רבי יהושע's view, not at the verse.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But isn't it written…?' Brings a verse as a challenge
Also / too

phrases.english: And for Rabbi Yehoshua too,
isn't it written: 'And the blood of your offerings shall be poured out'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי אליעזר's verse from Step 24 against רבי יהושע's view from Step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's view that both blood and meat must be valid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'ודם זבחיך ישפך' presents the blood as the main part of the offering. That suggests blood alone is enough, against רבי יהושע.

steps.title: The same verse also says: eat the meat
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע answers that the same verse continues 'והבשר תאכל', which shows that the meat also matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: right next to it, it is written, 'and you shall eat the meat.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers on behalf of רבי יהושע. It points to the second half of the same verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse does not stop after the blood. It goes on to say 'והבשר תאכל', so the meat is also an important part of the offering. That is why רבי יהושע still requires valid meat for the blood to work.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He would tell you', an answer given for someone's view
Next to it / with it
'And you shall eat the meat'

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר: blood alone brings כפרה ('ודם זבחיך ישפך'). רבי יהושע: both blood and meat are needed ('הבשר והדם', and 'והבשר תאכל' in the same verse).
steps.whyThisMatters: This confirms רבי יהושע's view from Step 23. That view is what drives the suggestion that our משנה goes against רבי יהושע.

phrases.english: He would say to you:
it is written right next to it: 'and you shall eat the meat.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the full verse in context
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse makes blood alone the main part, so רבי יהושע has no answer to it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The same verse also says 'והבשר תאכל', so the meat is required too, as רבי יהושע holds.
